svg.title: Making time for a shared activity

text.tspan: Everyday English - B1 - 2026/06/20 - 01 - Essay
A family spends time together.
Pexels · 5276077
Making time for a shared activity
There is more than one way to spend time with someone who cares for us. In my experience, practical preparation
and attention to others are two useful starting points.
One reason is that a simple shared activity creates space for conversation. For instance, we choose a short walk that
suits everyone’s pace. This prevents a small difficulty from taking over the experience. It also leaves us more time to
notice what is happening.
Another reason is that attention matters more than an elaborate plan. For example, we put our phones away and ask
about a familiar memory. This approach recognises that the experience belongs to more than one person and that
different people may need different things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to control every detail.
We can make a sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete
example. Conclude by connecting the two reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write
about an experience of your own.
Make a sentence of your own, then answer: What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example. (Model: The two
reasons are that a simple shared activity creates space for conversation and that attention matters more than an elaborate
plan. One example is that we choose a short walk that suits everyone’s pace.)
